A note about gender diversity

Some hair loss conditions are genetically predisposed to the gender that you were assigned at birth.

Even if you do not identify as either male or female it is important to know this information to create an accurate diagnosis.

If you were not assigned either 'male' or 'female' at birth, or feel that you still cannot accurately answer this question, then you can call our Clinical team to directly book a Consultation with a Trichologist.

You do not have to discuss your gender on the call and all conversations are treated as strictly confidential.

Itching:Itching can accompany many other scalp conditions, but if you have no visible redness, inflammation, dandruff or flakes but your scalp feels itchy select this
Dandruff:Dandruff has varying degrees of severity, ranging from mild common dandruff, i.e. loose flakes, to more severe forms like seborrheic dermatitis. Common dandruff is a non-inflammatory scalp condition. It should not cause redness, unless you are scratching your scalp repeatedly. If your scalp is red, you may have a different scalp condition
Eczema:Eczema often causes small, round, flat and hard skin surfaces that have almost a leathery look. It can come with flaking, redness and itching as well.
Redness: Redness is usually caused by an inflammatory skin condition, characterised by red blotches and papules. You may also experience visible blood vessels and scaly patches.
Psoriasis:Typically causes tight, thick, white, asbestos-like plaques. Unlike dandruff, these scales are usually red with bleeding points underneath them. If you have psoriasis on your scalp, it often occurs elsewhere on the body as well.
Pimples, spots or acne:Scalp pimples, spots, or acne may appear as red bumps, whiteheads, or blackheads, often causing tenderness, itching, or discomfort when touched or brushed against.

If you're experiencing symptoms on your scalp, it's important that we treat your scalp symptoms before we look to treat your hair loss. If we treat your hair loss while you're experiencing scalp irritation, it can make your scalp symptoms worse, and your hair loss treatments will be less effective. In mild-moderate scalp symptoms, we can typically clear these up in a few weeks and then get you on the right hair loss treatment plan.

If you're not having issues with your scalp, please remain on this assessment and select 'I don't have any of these symptoms' to continue.

Welcome, let's get started

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT?

Book your first Consultation with your Trichologist

Due to the nature of your hair loss, one of our world-renowned Trichologists will need to see you in a Consultation to confirm your diagnosis and prescribe a more suitable treatment plan for you.

You can book an In-Clinic Initial Consultation or a Virtual Inital Consultation with us by following the steps below.

What does a Consultation involve?

Philip Kingsley Virtual Consultation takes place via video call. Your Consultation lasts between 45-60 minutes, giving your Trichologist time to explore all factors affecting your hair and scalp; such as general health, diet and lifestyle, and your medical and family history.

Where is the Clinic located?

Our London Clinic is located in the heart of Mayfair. You can find us at 54 Green Street, London, W1K 6RU.

What's the difference between In-Clinic and Virtual Consultations?

Our In-Clinic Consultations are the most in-depth and accurate Consultations as we can thoroughly assess your hair & scalp with the tools we have at the Clinic. Our In-Clinic Consultations are also followed by a Treatment to treat your hair & scalp immediately after seeing our Trichologists. 

Our Virtual Consultations are a video call with one of our Trichologists. We will still take a full history and assess the photos of your hair & sclap you share with us before, but we can't guarantee a diagnosis on the call and wemay suggest you need a visit to the Clinic for a full diagnosis. You will however, still get access to our full range of exclusive treatment plans.
